added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(\varepsilon\leq\lambda_{n,\mathcal R}\leq1-\varepsilon\) for every \(n\).  On a joint probability space whose observed-data marginal is \(\mathbb P_n\), let \(G_n\sim N(0,\Gamma_n)\), and write \(\mathbb P_n\) also for the coupled law.  Suppose there is a deterministic sequence \(a_n\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
 \left|
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,k}-\tau_n)
 -(\beta_{n,k}+G_{n,k})
 \right|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1), \tag{1}
\]
and define
\[
 R_n=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
       |\widehat C_{n,k}-Q_{n,k}(G_n)|,
 \qquad
 \mathcal M_n(a)=
 \left\{k\in\mathcal K_n:
 Q_{n,k}(G_n)\leq
 \min_{l\in\mathcal K_n}Q_{n,l}(G_n)+2a
 \right\},
\]
\[
 D_n(a)=\max_{k,l\in\mathcal M_n(a)}d_n(k,l).
\]
If
\[
 \mathbb P_n(R_n\leq a_n)\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad
 D_n(a_n)\sqrt{\log(e|\mathcal K_n|)}
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1), \tag{2}
\]
then the bounded-Lipschitz distance between the law of
\(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)\) and the law of
\(\beta_{n,J_n(G_n)}+G_{n,J_n(G_n)}\) tends to zero.  This is a conditional transfer result only: it does not assert that (1)--(2) hold for the generated fixed-cardinality prefix estimator.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(J_n=J_n(G_n)\).  On the event \(\{R_n\leq a_n\}\), optimality of \(\widehat k_n\) for \(\widehat C_n\) and of \(J_n\) for \(Q_n(G_n)\) gives, equation by equation,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_{n,\widehat k_n}(G_n)
 &\leq \widehat C_{n,\widehat k_n}+a_n
 &&\text{by the definition of \(R_n\)},\\
 &\leq \widehat C_{n,J_n}+a_n
 &&\text{by the definition of \(\widehat k_n\)},\\
 &\leq Q_{n,J_n}(G_n)+2a_n
 &&\text{by the definition of \(R_n\)},\\
 &=\min_{l\in\mathcal K_n}Q_{n,l}(G_n)+2a_n
 &&\text{by the definition of \(J_n\)}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{3}
\]
Thus \(\widehat k_n\in\mathcal M_n(a_n)\); also \(J_n\in\mathcal M_n(a_n)\) directly from the definition of that set.  Consequently,
\[
 d_n(\widehat k_n,J_n)\leq D_n(a_n) \tag{4}
\]
on \(\{R_n\leq a_n\}\).

For deterministic \(k,l\in\mathcal K_n\), the definition of \(d_n\) gives
\[
 |\beta_{n,k}-\beta_{n,l}|\leq d_n(k,l), \tag{5}
\]
and the definition of \(G_n\), followed by the covariance identity in the definition of \(d_n\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}(G_{n,k}-G_{n,l})
 &=\Gamma_n(k,k)+\Gamma_n(l,l)-2\Gamma_n(k,l)\\
 &\leq d_n(k,l)^2. 
 \end{aligned} \tag{6}
\]
Equation (6) remains valid when \(\Gamma_n\) is singular.  Let \(m_n=|\mathcal K_n|\).  If \(d_n(k,l)\leq r\) for \(r>0\), then \(G_{n,k}-G_{n,l}\) is a centered Gaussian variable with variance at most \(r^2\).  Its moment-generating function is at most \(\exp(t^2r^2/2)\).  On the event \(\{G_{n,k}-G_{n,l}>u\}\), the nonnegative variable \(\exp\{t(G_{n,k}-G_{n,l})\}\) is at least \(e^{tu}\); hence, for \(u>0\),
\[
 \mathbb P_n(G_{n,k}-G_{n,l}>u)
 \leq \exp\{-tu+t^2r^2/2\}.
\]
Minimizing at \(t=u/r^2\), applying the same argument to the negative tail, and then taking a union bound over at most \(m_n^2\) ordered pairs yields, for every \(x>0\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathbb P_n\Bigg[
 \max_{\substack{k,l\in\mathcal K_n\\d_n(k,l)\leq r}}
 |(\beta_{n,k}+G_{n,k})-(\beta_{n,l}+G_{n,l})|\\
 >r+r\sqrt{2\{\log(2m_n^2)+x\}}
 \Bigg]\leq e^{-x}. 
 \end{split} \tag{7}
\]
Here (5) accounts for the first \(r\) on the threshold.  If \(r=0\), both differences in (5)--(6) vanish almost surely, so (7) is immediate by continuity.

Let \(L_n=\log(em_n)\).  The second condition in (2) implies that there is a deterministic sequence \(c_n>0\), \(c_n\downarrow0\), for which
\[
 \mathbb P_n\{D_n(a_n)\sqrt{L_n}>c_n\}\longrightarrow0. \tag{8}
\]
Indeed, this is the standard diagonal characterization of convergence in probability: choose successive positive thresholds tending to zero after indices at which their exceedance probabilities are at most the thresholds.  Set \(r_n=c_n/\sqrt{L_n}\).  Then
\[
 \mathbb P_n\{D_n(a_n)>r_n\}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 r_n\sqrt{L_n}=c_n\longrightarrow0. \tag{9}
\]
The sampling-fraction condition and \(n_{\mathcal E}=n(1-\lambda_{n,\mathcal R})\) imply
\[
 m_n=n_{\mathcal E}+1\geq\varepsilon n+1\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
so \(L_n\to\infty\).  Apply (7) with \(r=r_n\) and \(x=L_n\).  Since \(\log(2m_n^2)\leq2L_n+\log2\), the probability bound \(e^{-L_n}\) tends to zero and the threshold in (7) is \(O(r_n\sqrt{L_n})=O(c_n)=o(1)\).  Equations (4), (8)--(9), and \(\mathbb P_n(R_n\leq a_n)\to1\) therefore imply
\[
 (\beta_{n,\widehat k_n}+G_{n,\widehat k_n})
 -(\beta_{n,J_n}+G_{n,J_n})=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{10}
\]

Evaluating the maximum in (1) at the data-dependent index \(\widehat k_n\) gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)
 -(\beta_{n,\widehat k_n}+G_{n,\widehat k_n})
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{11}
\]
Combining (10) and (11),
\[
 \Delta_n:=
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)
 -(\beta_{n,J_n(G_n)}+G_{n,J_n(G_n)})
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{12}
\]
For every real function \(f\) bounded by one and with Lipschitz constant at most one, the coupling and (12) give
\[
 \left|E f(X_n)-E f(Y_n)\right|
 \leq E\min\{2,|\Delta_n|\}, \tag{13}
\]
where \(X_n\) and \(Y_n\) are the two variables in (12).  For every \(u>0\), the right side of (13) is at most
\[
 u+2\mathbb P_n(|\Delta_n|>u),
\]
which tends to at most \(u\) by (12), and then to zero as \(u\downarrow0\).  Taking the supremum over the bounded-Lipschitz class proves the claimed convergence of laws.
added_lemmas.justification: This lemma preserves the valid selection-transfer argument while making its Gaussian coupling and quantitative near-minimizer stability explicit hypotheses.
added_lemmas.gap: It is a conditional mathematical transfer, not an achievability result for the generated fixed-cardinality prefix path.
added_lemmas.consumer: A future primitive rank-boundary process theorem can use it in a justified Gaussian subregime; a non-Gaussian corrected process requires the analogous direct transfer.

added_lemmas.statement:
Two distinct obstructions hold, on separate witnesses.  First, for an admissible choice of the fixed constants, there exist a sequence \(\mathbf P^{\mathrm B}\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\) and deterministic interior prefixes \(k_n^{\mathrm B}/n_{\mathcal E}\to1/2\) such that
\[
 S_n^{\mathrm B}:=
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k_n^{\mathrm B}}-\tau_n-b_{n,k_n^{\mathrm B}}\}
\]
has a non-Gaussian subsequential limit.  Consequently the frozen all-prefix coupling to \(G_n\sim N(0,\Gamma_n)\) fails, and no repair that changes only the covariance of a centered Gaussian process can couple this coordinate with \(o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\) error.

Second, suppose \(\lambda\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), \(t\in(0,1]\), and \(\sigma_0^2,\sigma_1^2>0\).  Define
\[
 A_{\max}=\frac{2\sqrt2\,\sigma_0}{t\varepsilon^{3/2}},
\]
and suppose
\[
 \frac{\sigma_0^q+\sigma_1^q}{2}\leq\frac C2,
 \qquad
 A_{\max}\leq\min\{C,(C/2)^{1/q}\}.
\]
Then the separate finite-support construction gives a sequence \(\mathbf P^{\mathrm T}\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\) for which, for every sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \rho_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=\rho_{n,0},
 \qquad
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)>0,
 \qquad
 \omega^{\star}(0)>0.
\]
Thus exact leading-risk tie invariance fails.  These two conclusions do not assert that the generated selector chooses the non-Gaussian coordinate, and they do not establish or refute any particular selected marginal limit law.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The first witness is the one proved in \(\mathrm{thm:generated\text{-}prefix\text{-}coupling}\).  That theorem supplies \(\mathbf P^{\mathrm B}\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\), a deterministic interior prefix \(k_n^{\mathrm B}\), and a subsequence along which
\[
 S_n^{\mathrm B}\ \Rightarrow\ S^{\mathrm B}, \tag{14}
\]
where \(S^{\mathrm B}\) is non-Gaussian.  If the frozen all-prefix coupling held, retaining its single \(k_n^{\mathrm B}\) coordinate would give
\[
 |S_n^{\mathrm B}-G_{n,k_n^{\mathrm B}}|
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{15}
\]
For every real function \(f\) bounded by one and with Lipschitz constant at most one, (15) would imply
\[
 \left|E f(S_n^{\mathrm B})-E f(G_{n,k_n^{\mathrm B}})\right|
 \leq E\min\{2,|S_n^{\mathrm B}-G_{n,k_n^{\mathrm B}}|\}
 \longrightarrow0, \tag{16}
\]
because for every \(u>0\) the expectation on the right is at most
\[
 u+2\mathbb P_n\{|S_n^{\mathrm B}-G_{n,k_n^{\mathrm B}}|>u\}.
\]
The established theorem already proves that (15) is impossible for its frozen Gaussian coordinate; hence (16) contradicts its established non-Gaussian subsequential limit.  This is the asserted failure of the frozen coupling.

The same argument rules out a covariance-only Gaussian repair.  Suppose instead that, on the subsequence in (14), centered Gaussian variables \(Z_n\sim N(0,v_n)\), with arbitrary \(v_n\geq0\), satisfied
\[
 |S_n^{\mathrm B}-Z_n|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{17}
\]
By (14), \(S_n^{\mathrm B}\) is tight.  Equation (17) then makes \(Z_n\) tight, because
\[
 \mathbb P_n(|Z_n|>M+1)
 \leq \mathbb P_n(|S_n^{\mathrm B}|>M)
 +\mathbb P_n(|S_n^{\mathrm B}-Z_n|>1).
\]
A family \(N(0,v_n)\) is tight only if \(\sup_n v_n<\infty\); otherwise, for every fixed \(M>0\), a subsequence with \(v_n\to\infty\) would satisfy \(\mathbb P(|Z_n|\leq M)\to0\).  Passing to a further subsequence, let \(v_n\to v\geq0\).  If \(v=0\), then, for every \(\eta>0\),
\[
 \eta^2\mathbb P_n(|Z_n|>\eta)\leq E[Z_n^2]=v_n\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus \(Z_n=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\), so (17) makes \(S_n^{\mathrm B}=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\), contradicting the non-Gaussian limit in (14).  If \(v>0\), then for every \(x\in\mathbb R\) and \(\delta>0\),
\[
 \mathbb P_n(Z_n\leq x-\delta)-\mathbb P_n(|S_n^{\mathrm B}-Z_n|>\delta)
 \leq \mathbb P_n(S_n^{\mathrm B}\leq x)
 \leq \mathbb P_n(Z_n\leq x+\delta)+\mathbb P_n(|S_n^{\mathrm B}-Z_n|>\delta). \tag{18}
\]
At every continuity point \(x\) of the distribution function of \(S^{\mathrm B}\), first let \(n\to\infty\) in (18), using (14), (17), and
\[
 \mathbb P_n(Z_n\leq y)=\Phi(y/\sqrt{v_n})\longrightarrow\Phi(y/\sqrt v),
\]
and then let \(\delta\downarrow0\).  Continuity of \(\Phi\) gives
\[
 \mathbb P(S^{\mathrm B}\leq x)=\Phi(x/\sqrt v).
\]
Distribution functions are right-continuous and their continuity points are dense, so this equality determines the law of \(S^{\mathrm B}\) as \(N(0,v)\), again contradicting (14).  Hence changing only the covariance of a Gaussian process cannot repair the boundary coordinate.  The established witness identifies the omitted term as the empirical fixed-cardinality quantile-boundary term and proves that it is non-Gaussian.

For the second conclusion, the stated positivity and moment inequalities are exactly the feasibility premises of \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}support\text{-}tie\text{-}witness}\).  That theorem proves that its different construction belongs to \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\) and that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \rho_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=\rho_{n,0},
 \qquad
 d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)^2
 \geq B_n^2(a_n^{\dagger})^2
 \longrightarrow D_\infty>0. \tag{19}
\]
All quantities in (19) are nonnegative, so taking square roots gives
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)
 \geq\sqrt{D_\infty}>0. \tag{20}
\]
The same theorem applies the definition of the selection modulus to the exact equalities in (19) and obtains
\[
 \omega^{\star}(0)\geq\sqrt{D_\infty}>0. \tag{21}
\]
Equations (19)--(21) prove failure of exact leading-risk tie invariance.  The first and second established theorems use different law sequences, and none of (14)--(21) analyzes the random event that \(\widehat k_n\) selects a particular coordinate.  Therefore no conclusion about the selected marginal law has been drawn.
added_lemmas.justification: This theorem records the faithful negative boundary using two separate witnesses: one for rank-boundary non-Gaussianity and one for exact-risk-tie target separation.
added_lemmas.gap: Fixed-prefix asymptotic normality does not represent the empirical fixed-cardinality boundary, while equality of leading risks does not control the distance between causal estimator coordinates.
added_lemmas.consumer: It blocks use of the frozen covariance process in the selected-law and multiplier-interval problems without claiming that any selected marginal law has itself been disproved.

added_lemmas.statement:
For the actual generated fixed-cardinality prefix path, which primitive score-index regularity conditions and estimator-side entropy or near-minimizer conditions suffice to derive, uniformly over \(k\in\mathcal K_n\), the joint law of
\[
 \left(
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k}-\tau_n-b_{n,k}\},
 \widehat C_{n,k}
 \right)_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
\]
from the displayed sample maps?  The corrected process must include both the external empirical-quantile boundary term created by fixed-cardinality ranking and the trial-sample derivative induced by replacing \(s_n(z)\) with \(\widehat s_n(z)\).  Derive from those primitive conditions a quantitative near-minimizer bound strong enough to invoke \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}quadratic\text{-}transfer}\), or prove the corresponding transfer directly, and state the resulting bounded-Lipschitz law of \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)\) across fixed, vanishing, and exact gaps.  On \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\) the corrected boundary process must be allowed to be non-Gaussian; a Gaussian correction may be asserted only under independently justified score-index smoothness.  Neither the desired coupling nor the near-minimizer conclusion may be imposed as a headline assumption.
added_lemmas.justification: The selected-estimator law is not established until the actual ranked functional, rather than its frozen-threshold surrogate, is linearized and its near minimizers are controlled.
added_lemmas.gap: The current primitive class has a score-density margin but no score-index smoothness that rules out a nonlinear empirical-quantile boundary term, and it has no primitive all-prefix entropy or stability theorem.
added_lemmas.consumer: Its resolution is the prerequisite for a computable multiplier interval uniformly valid across fixed, vanishing, and exact gaps.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The unconditional frozen-covariance quadratic law is unsupported and its requisite coordinate coupling is refuted by the proved regular-class fixed-cardinality witness.  The replacement keeps the actual selected law as a precise primitive research obligation, while the valid conditional transfer and the two negative witness facts are preserved in separate proved nodes.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: The causal estimand remains \(\tau_n=E_{P_n}[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid R=1]\), and \(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}\) is a sample-selected estimator aimed at that estimand, not a definition of it.  The current core does not establish an unconditional weak law for \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)\).  The proved conditional transfer lemma yields the displayed Gaussian-quadratic coordinate only after its joint Gaussian coupling and quantitative near-minimizer condition have independently been established.  The boundary-obstruction theorem proves that the frozen \(\Gamma_n\) process, and any covariance-only Gaussian repair, cannot provide that coupling on the present regular class because a first-order fixed-cardinality boundary term may be non-Gaussian.  It does not prove that the selected marginal law fails; identifying the rank-boundary-corrected process and selected law is the formal open question.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The former field still displayed a selected Gaussian-quadratic law whose frozen coupling is invalid.  This replacement separates the causal target, estimator, proved conditional transfer, negative coupling obstruction, and genuinely unestablished selected limit.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem~2 gives \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) MSE estimation for any given borrowed set, and Theorem~3 gives selection consistency for a given influence ranking under a fixed positive separation.
Theorem~1 gives asymptotic normality of a fixed-prefix estimator after centering by its prefix-specific bias.
Theorems~2.3 and~3.1 show local nonuniform impossibility for estimating post-model-selection distributions in broad nested and AIC-like selection problems.
Theorem~3 derives a local focused-selection law and Theorem~4 guarantees coverage at least \(1-\alpha-\gamma\) for a fixed invalid-instrument selection problem.
Theorem~3.1 characterizes ordinary-bootstrap validity by full differentiability under a Gaussian limit, and Theorem~3.2 validates derivative-aware resampling.
The sorting operator is Hadamard differentiable at regular values and yields a uniform sorted-process central limit theorem and bootstrap bands on compact interior quantile sets.
Theorems~2.1 and~2.6 give Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap approximations for maxima of high-dimensional sample-mean vectors under sub-exponential or polynomial moments.
Theorem~1 gives selective coverage by simultaneous inference over a data-dependent set of locally plausible targets.
Conditional truncated-Gaussian and hybrid projection procedures correct the winner's curse when a target coordinate is selected by optimizing noisy estimates.
Theorem~2.3 gives exact Fisher-randomization-test size under a sharp null, and Theorem~3.5 gives an excess-risk bound for an adaptive conformal borrowing threshold.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The project no longer claims a positive simultaneous extension of the fixed-prefix theory.  The formal non-representability comparison is delivered by the proved obstruction theorem, not by the open corrected-local-gap question.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Derive from primitive score-index and complexity conditions the rank-boundary-corrected joint estimator and criterion process for the actual generated fixed-cardinality prefixes, then derive the selected-estimator law across fixed, vanishing, and exact gaps.
open_obligations.obstruction: A density margin alone permits outcome behavior oscillating at the empirical rank-boundary scale.  The resulting boundary functional can be nonlinear and non-Gaussian, while the frozen estimated influence values omit it.  The class also supplies neither score-index differentiability for the generated ranking nor an all-prefix entropy or primitive near-minimizer theorem.
open_obligations.attempted: The frozen-threshold Gaussian influence coupling and a covariance-only correction were tested and refuted by the regular-class boundary witness.  The deterministic argmin transfer was isolated and proved conditionally, but its coupling and stability hypotheses cannot be inferred from the present primitives.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The strongest established facts are a negative boundary and a conditional transfer.  The regular-class witness in \(\mathrm{thm:frozen\text{-}prefix\text{-}boundary\text{-}obstruction}\) gives an interior deterministic prefix for which
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k_n}-\tau_n-b_{n,k_n}\}
 \Rightarrow Z+H(X),
\]
where \(Z\) is Gaussian and \(H(X)\) is a bounded, nonconstant, non-Gaussian empirical-quantile boundary contribution.  Thus the fixed-threshold \(\Gamma_n\)-Gaussian process and every covariance-only Gaussian repair are invalid for that coordinate.  A separate legal finite-support witness has
\[
 \rho_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=\rho_{n,0},
 \qquad
 \liminf_n d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)>0,
\]
so exact risk ties are not target-coordinate ties.  Finally, \(\mathrm{lem:conditional\text{-}quadratic\text{-}transfer}\) proves that any correctly coupled joint process yields a selected bounded-Lipschitz law once its random near-minimizer set has \(d_n\)-diameter \(o_{\mathbb P_n}(1/\sqrt{\log(e|\mathcal K_n|)})\).  What remains is to derive the corrected process and this stability from primitive score-index and complexity conditions for the actual estimator.

prose_updates.tldr: Influence-ranked external-control borrowing is a focused selection problem with a generated fixed-cardinality ranking and a squared estimated-bias criterion.  The proved headline is a negative boundary, not a selected-limit theorem: on the regular continuous-score class, the frozen fixed-threshold influence process omits a first-order empirical rank-boundary term that can be non-Gaussian, so its all-prefix Gaussian coupling and every covariance-only Gaussian repair fail.  Separately, a bounded no-covariate squared-loss construction gives legal nested prefixes with exactly equal leading MSE but separated root-\(n\) ATE coordinates, so \(\omega^{\star}(0)>0\).  A conditional transfer lemma is proved, but the rank-boundary-corrected joint process, the selected law, the sharp excess modulus, and a computable tie-uniform multiplier interval remain open.

project_justification.fill: The project proves a non-representability boundary for the attempted frozen-covariance all-prefix extension, proves on a separate legal witness that exact leading-risk ties can retain first-order ATE-coordinate separation, and isolates a rigorous conditional near-minimizer transfer lemma.  It does not claim an unconditional quadratic law for the generated selector.  The named remaining problem is to derive from primitive conditions the rank-boundary-corrected joint estimator and criterion process, allowing a non-Gaussian boundary process on the current class unless additional score-index smoothness justifies a Gaussian correction, together with primitive near-minimizer or entropy control before tie-uniform inference is constructed.

prose_updates.related_work: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang define the influence score in equation~(3), the nested top-\(k\) workflow in Algorithm~1, fixed-prefix bias and Gaussian behavior in Theorem~1, pointwise MSE estimation in Theorem~2, and given-ranking fixed-gap selection consistency in Theorem~3.  The present obstruction shows that those fixed-prefix results do not represent the generated fixed-cardinality all-prefix path through the frozen fixed-threshold covariance \(\Gamma_n\): the empirical quantile boundary contributes at first order and may be non-Gaussian.  Claeskens and Hjort supply the local-misspecification and focused-risk architecture, including the non-estimability of local bias.  Patel, DiTraglia, Zuber, and Burgess derive focused-selector inference for a fixed invalid-instrument problem, but their candidate list is not generated by estimated individual ranks.  Leeb and Poetscher provide the generic local nonuniformity background for selection.  Fang and Santos explain failure of ordinary resampling at nondifferentiable maps and motivate derivative-aware resampling.  Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val, and Luo derive regular-value sorting derivatives, but the present class does not impose the score-index smoothness needed to turn every rank-boundary contribution into a Gaussian linear correction.  Chernozhukov and coauthors provide orthogonal fixed-target expansions, while Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Kato, and Koike provide Gaussian and multiplier approximations for high-dimensional sample-mean vectors; neither removes the need to derive the correct ranked functional first.  Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen, Zrnic and Fithian, and Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey provide localization or optimization-selection architectures that become applicable only after that process is identified.  Zhu, Yang, and Wang study exact sharp-null randomization validity and conformal threshold borrowing, not a superpopulation weak-null ATE interval for this generated influence-ranked selector.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The local-risk coordinate is the \(n\)-scaled MSE under \(n^{-1/2}\) exchangeability violations.  The legal exact-tie witness may contain score atoms and therefore need not lie in the regular margin class.  The separate coupling witness does lie in the regular class and has a continuous score, but its score-indexed outcome oscillates at the empirical rank-boundary scale; the resulting fixed-cardinality boundary term is non-Gaussian.  Thus a density margin alone is insufficient.  A positive selected-law theorem needs a primitive linearization of both the external empirical-quantile boundary and the trial-generated score perturbation, plus smoothness or other structure controlling score-indexed conditional contributions and quantitative stability of random near minimizers.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The established headline consists of two separate negative facts: the frozen \(\Gamma_n\)-Gaussian all-prefix coupling and every covariance-only Gaussian repair fail on a regular continuous-score fixed-cardinality witness, while exact leading-MSE ties can have nonvanishing ATE-coordinate distance on a different legal witness.  Neither fact establishes or refutes the selected marginal law, because the first witness does not prove that the selector chooses its non-Gaussian coordinate.  The conditional quadratic transfer lemma is proved but is not an achievability theorem for the actual generated selector.  The formal remaining obligation is to derive from primitive conditions a rank-boundary-corrected joint estimator and criterion process, allowing a non-Gaussian boundary term on the current class unless additional score-index smoothness justifies a Gaussian correction, and to prove sufficient near-minimizer or entropy control.  The sharp excess modulus on restricted prefix-Gram subclasses and the computable tie-uniform multiplier interval remain open.  The fixed-gap and no-borrowing propositions remain conditional sanity checks and carry no generated-path novelty claim.

statement_notes.justification: This lemma preserves the valid selection-transfer argument without asserting that its coupling and stability hypotheses follow from the current generated-ranking class.
statement_notes.gap: The unresolved mathematical work lies in establishing a correct process and primitive stability, not in the deterministic argmin comparison.
statement_notes.consumer: It transfers a future justified Gaussian rank-boundary process to the selected estimator; a non-Gaussian process requires the corresponding direct version.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem gives the faithful negative headline while explicitly keeping the non-Gaussian boundary witness separate from the exact-risk-tie witness.
statement_notes.gap: Fixed-prefix theory omits empirical rank-boundary behavior, and leading-risk equality alone does not imply target-coordinate equality.
statement_notes.consumer: It determines why the frozen process cannot calibrate the selected law or multiplier interval, without overclaiming that the selected marginal law is disproved.

statement_notes.justification: This question states the exact primitive work needed before any unconditional selected-estimator limit can be claimed.
statement_notes.gap: The current class lacks score-index differentiability and all-prefix stability sufficient to derive the missing boundary process.
statement_notes.consumer: Its resolution is required before the localized multiplier interval can be calibrated uniformly over all gap regimes.
